predecessors.name: Regency of Algiers
predecessors.text: the unoccupied Oran province, recognised to Abd al-Qadir by the Treaty of Desmichels in 1834 (and, from 1837, 'approximately two thirds of Algeria')

successors.name: French Algeria
successors.text: the whole country, as Cliopatria's French Algeria row (211,876 km2) draws it from 1846

ledger.x: 27 November 1832: the Emirate of Abdelkader is established.
1835: the capital moves from Mascara to Tagdemt.

ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)
Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 30 May 1837: France recognises 'approximately two thirds of Algeria' as Abdelkader's, in exchange for his recognising French sovereignty; the provinces of Oran, Koléa, Médéa, Tlemcen and Algiers are named, France keeps its major ports and Constantine is taken by France on 13 October 1837.

ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 1846: the fighting ends in the interior.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 1846: the last of the Emirate's ground passes to French Algeria.

wars.name: Desmichels and Tafna phase of the French conquest of Algeria
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Desmichels (26 February 1834) recognised Abdelkader in the Oran province; the Treaty of Tafna (30 May 1837) recognised him over 'approximately two thirds of Algeria' and left France its ports.

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria, last phase
wars.outcome: After the Iron Gates passage of late 1839 and Bugeaud's scorched-earth campaigns (from December 1840), the Smala was raided in 1843, Abdelkader's influence in the east was ended in 1845-1846 and he surrendered on 23 December 1847.

wars.name: First Franco-Moroccan War
wars.outcome: The French used military means in 1844 to compel the sultan; the 1844 Treaty of Tangier had Morocco outlaw the Emir from its kingdom.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Tafna 'defined the limits of its dominion' in the Oran and Algiers provinces according to a footnote, but no page gives a line; every frontier is approximate.
